clue.text: Stamp equity shares for Admiralty bigwigs

parts.note: to stamp a document is to seal it
ordinary shares, the commonest equity shares, are called ords in City slang

explanation.surface: A trader stamps share certificates bound for senior naval officials.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sea Lords are the senior naval officers who sit on the Admiralty Board in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior naval officers on Britain's Admiralty Board carry this title, so they are its top brass.

clue.text: Household god for instance without pay

indicators.note: here without has its old sense of outside, so the phrase for instance goes around the god

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example, as for instance is
a lar was one of the Roman gods of the home

explanation.surface: Even a household deity, it seems, goes unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is read in its old sense 'outside', so SAY wraps round LAR, a Roman household god, giving SA-LAR-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular wages for a job are its fixed remuneration, a synonym.

clue.text: A student master chess champion of the eid school

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation, standing for a student
MA, Master of Arts, is a master's degree
one who mates the opposing king is a mater, the winner of a chess game

explanation.surface: A student with a master's degree turns out to be a chess champion of the traditional kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A chess game is won by giving mate, so the winner is literally a 'mater'. The page's 'eid' is an OCR slip for 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, meaning nourishing mother, is used for the school or college a person once attended.

clue.text: Hobby without profit

parts.note: without in its old sense means outside
interest is the profit earned on money lent

explanation.surface: A pastime that earns nothing is still worth pursuing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit kept up apart from one's work is a pastime, a synonym for a hobby.

clue.text: Old-fashioned rally faded away when I was excluded

parts.note: a demo, a demonstration, is a protest rally

indicators.note: the letter I is said to be left out of the word for faded away

parts.note: to die away is to fade away

explanation.surface: A protest rally fizzled out after one speaker was left off the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was excluded' takes I out of DIED, leaving DED after DEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Démodé is a French borrowing for out of style, the same as outdated.

clue.text: Carry a loss-leader In entrance

parts.note: to port a weapon is to carry it

indicators.note: the leader of the word loss is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shop lugs a cut-price loss-leader through its doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss-leader' reads as the shop's bargain line, but it is the first letter of 'loss'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand doorway or gateway is a portal, a synonym for an entrance.

clue.text: What one might do for Customs examination is a foregone conclusion

definitions.text: What one might do for Customs examination
definitions.meaning: a traveller at Customs might open a suitcase and then shut it again
a matter whose outcome is obvious from the start

explanation.surface: The bag check at Customs was a matter whose result everyone knew in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a suitcase opened and closed for inspection, and an idiom for a matter needing no deliberation.

clue.text: Lash with a lisping air

indicators.note: a lisp turns an S sound into TH, so the word for air is said that way

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A whip crack accompanied by a lisped melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lisping' turns the S of SONG into TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a strip of leather used as a whip, so it can mean a lash.

clue.text: University exam for those with not much leave

parts.note: little means not much
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A college test for staff granted little time off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Little Go was the old name for Cambridge University's preliminary examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge's former entrance-stage test, the Previous Examination, was known by this name.

clue.text: His clients find him extremely interesting

definitions.text: His clients find him extremely interesting

parts.words: His clients find him extremely interesting
parts.note: interesting is read as charging interest: a moneylender's borrowers find his rates very high

explanation.surface: A professional whose customers find him fascinating company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interesting' looks like praise but means 'charging interest', and a lender charging excessive interest is the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging exorbitant interest is exactly someone whose borrowers find him high in interest.

clue.text: Illuminated motorway inside border

indicators.note: the motorway letter goes inside the word for illuminated

parts.note: lit means illuminated
motorway gives MI

explanation.surface: A lit motorway runs through the land at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'herder' is an OCR slip for 'border'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary line marks where something ends, as an edge or bound does.

clue.text: Skips with girls abroad

parts.note: misses are young unmarried women
out means away from home, abroad

explanation.surface: Someone skips off with young women to foreign parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out by passing over it is to omit it, a synonym of skips.

clue.text: Second application about a rest

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the second application goes round the letter A

parts.note: a reminder is a second request, as for an unpaid bill

explanation.surface: A second request comes in about getting some rest.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over is the balance, a synonym of rest.

clue.text: Obliging person to be a dramale backer

definitions.meaning: a kind, helpful person is called an ...
a financial backer of a theatrical show

explanation.surface: A kindly soul who puts money into plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a very kind helper and an investor in a stage production.

clue.text: An abstainer given close escort

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone abstaining from alcohol
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is given a tight bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to accompany them, as an attendant does.

clue.text: Bird playing outside right for Russia?

parts.note: red stood for Soviet Russia, its flag and its army
in football the outside right plays on the wing

explanation.surface: A footballer playing on the right flank for the Russian team.
explanation.walkthrough: In older football terms the 'outside right' was the right winger. The redwing is a thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: A redwing is a thrush of northern Europe, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Not very original of one Frenchman with sex-appeal to bring up Evita

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is short for Monsieur
it is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing up a word means reading it from the bottom upward

explanation.surface: An unoriginal production of Evita staged by a seductive Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring up' reverses EVITA to ATIVE, as the entry runs downward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that copies others rather than inventing is derivative, lacking originality.

clue.text: Body grew older when rubbed the right way

parts.note: a mass is a body of matter
aged means grew older

explanation.surface: An ageing body is kneaded properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading muscles to soothe them is rubbing them skilfully, and the word also means soothed by flattery.

clue.text: Order soldiers to return cooker ()

indicators.note: returning sends the soldiers' letters back the other way

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, gives soldiers
a range is a kitchen stove

explanation.surface: Soldiers are ordered to bring back the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns RA (Royal Artillery) into AR, then RANGE follows. The empty brackets are where the page lost the letter count.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order is to organise them, a synonym.

clue.text: Make precious tip to hearing aid

parts.note: a tip is the end of something
the ear is the organ that aids hearing

explanation.surface: Advice about a hearing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone loved or dear to another is to cause them to be cherished.

clue.text: County girl embracing one joint beneficiary

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the girl wraps round the one

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a girl
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl from the shires hugs someone who shares an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inherits jointly with another shares an estate as a co-heir.

clue.text: Intimidate female's daughter with neat worker

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate
her is the possessive for a female

explanation.surface: A woman bullies her daughter, who works tidily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is an old word for cattle, so a neat worker tends cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means cattle, so someone tending cattle is a cattle hand.

clue.text: Determined camping

definitions.meaning: firmly resolved, set on a purpose
a camper sleeps under canvas, in a tent

explanation.surface: Resolute about holidays under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means resolved; the other, split as two words, means under canvas.

clue.text: Wrong returning for instance to burn

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for for instance is written backwards

explanation.surface: Wrongly returning for an example is a way to scorch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns EG round to GE. The page's 'stance' is an OCR slip for 'instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch slightly is to char the surface, a mild burn.

clue.text: Fabric from Northern Ireland? Not at all French

parts.note: non is French for no, not at all

explanation.surface: Is this cloth from Ulster? Certainly not, it is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a sheer lightweight silk or rayon cloth, an example of a fabric.

clue.text: Neath coach on 10.30 from Paddington

parts.note: 'neath, short for beneath, means down below
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A coach to Neath on the 10.30 out of Paddington.
explanation.walkthrough: Neath looks like the Welsh town served from Paddington, but it is 'neath, beneath. A train leaving London is a down train; Paddington is a London terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A service travelling away from London is called a down service, as one leaving Paddington does.

clue.text: One drink to put some pep into another

parts.note: to ginger something up is to give it more pep
ale is another drink

explanation.surface: Adding one drink to another to liven it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put some pep into' looks like an instruction to insert, but it means the verb 'ginger'.
explanation.definitionFit: This fizzy soft drink flavoured with root spice is an example of a drink.

clue.text: Quick article not recorded

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a live broadcast is not recorded

explanation.surface: A speedy item broadcast without a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' is the old sense, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: In its old sense quick means living, as in the quick and the dead.

clue.text: Give appointment on going inside

indicators.note: the word on goes inside the word for appointment

parts.note: a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: Give your appointment slot as you go in.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give something away as a gift.

clue.text: Notice chap letting money go to disciple

parts.note: an ad is a notice
he is a pronoun for a chap
rent is the money paid for letting property

explanation.surface: A notice that a man let his money go to a follower.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a cause or teacher supports it faithfully, as a disciple does.
